value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for breaking work into verbs with reusable patterns
value.lets_workers: Choose how to break work into verbs using common, reusable shapes, try alternative breakdowns as separate attempts, and keep the shape that led to better downstream results, with every pattern carrying its own success record.

flow.when: For a goal that may need more than one verb; one attempt per alternative.
Turns one breakdown into child task previews; a person or authorized requester enqueues them.
After the children of two or more attempts finish.
Last: add the result to the pattern's success record.

value.first_rule: Prefer single-verb. Split only when parts have independent outcomes, permissions or recovery.

value.title: Breakdown pattern: do it in one verb
value.category_reason: A breakdown pattern is a reusable, low-token plan shape distilled from work that went well; applying it needs no fresh planning.
value.summary: Keep the work as one verb when one worker can hold the context, there is one outcome, and no step needs different permissions.
use_when: One outcome and one acceptance check set.
Fits one worker's context and time limit.
No step needs a different permission or reviewer.
avoid_when: Parts can fail independently and should be retried alone.
A step needs a different permission, tool or reviewer.
stop_rules: Stop when the acceptance checks pass or the time limit is reached.
value.budget_rule: The whole breakdown shares one budget; children never get a fresh allowance of their own.

value.title: Breakdown pattern: probe first, then build
value.category_reason: A breakdown pattern is a reusable, low-token plan shape distilled from work that went well; applying it needs no fresh planning.
value.summary: Resolve the single unknown that decides the approach with a small time-boxed probe, then build only if the probe says it is feasible.
use_when: One key uncertainty decides whether the approach works at all.
The probe is much cheaper than the build.
avoid_when: The probe would cost as much as the build.

stages.note: Time-boxed; answers one yes or no question.
Starts only if the probe's outcome is feasible.

stop_rules: If the probe answers not feasible, finish with no_change.
The build must check the probe's actual outcome, not only that it finished.
value.budget_rule: The whole breakdown shares one budget; children never get a fresh allowance of their own.
failure_modes: The probe asks the wrong question.
A dependency on a finished but failed probe lets the build start anyway.
